title: PlunderSpell Changelog
eyebrow: Changelog · 23 September to 27 October 2026 · real screenshots only

short.lead: PlunderSpell, a co-op voice-spell heist game, from the first grey-box playtest on 23 September to staging on 27 October. Every picture already existed in the repo, and each caption names its file.
short.hint: The Changes tab is the changelog: Kept is built and checked, Changed is something that works differently now, New is being built or comes next.

changes: chg
Five weeks apart
From grey boxes to a lit castle and a modelled wizard.
23 September: grey boxes and a debug menu
8 October on: the wizard, cast and lit
The first playtest on 23 September already had the whole loop, in grey boxes. The wizard, the four Ages' castles and the night look came after.

before.alt: Grey-box room with a capsule guard on fire

after.alt: The modelled wizard casting in a stone vaulted room

changes: keep
Built 23 September: a playable raid in grey boxes
Spawn, cast by voice, fight, carry loot out, die or escape.
Milestones M0 (fork clean, cut gravity) and most of M1 (prove the voice). Voice recognition runs through Vosk, with a keyboard stand-in.

changes.alt: Grey-box room with a capsule guard on fire
changes.caption: docs/generated/playtest-2026-09-23/19-voice-ignis-burns-guard.png

changes: keep
Built 24 September to 6 October: four Ages, each its own castle
Bronze Age, High Medieval, Late Medieval and the Age of Powder.

Each Age builds from its own rooms. A night atmosphere, fog and a painted surface look replaced the flat grey. Castles stack a crypt, a ground floor and a keep, joined by stairs, with doors that lock when the alarm is raised.

changes.alt: The castle from outside at night, lit windows in the fog
changes.caption: docs/generated/ages-check-2026-10-06/HighMedieval/outside-south.png

changes: keep
Built 30 September to 3 October: guards rebuilt
Patrol, investigate, chase, fight in turns, search, give up.
A fresh guard brain with its own castle navigation. Guards answer the hue and cry, can be stunned, slept or set on fire, and climb stairs. Issues #203 to #223, #229 and #236 to #239.

changes.alt: Inside a High Medieval keep, fog and a wall torch
changes.caption: docs/generated/ages-check-2026-10-06/HighMedieval/keep-centre.png

changes: keep
Built early October: the art bible, 36 models
Every guard and every piece of loot across the four Ages, nine per Age.
Each model was built by the art pipeline with a review sheet. Shown: the Bronze Age gold death mask. The others are in docs/generated/art-bible-models/img/.

changes.alt: Model sheet of the Bronze Age gold death mask
changes.caption: docs/generated/art-bible-models/img/bronze-gold-death-mask.jpg

changes: keep
Built 7 October: the Lair and the Market as places
The Lair menu became a room you walk around.

The ledger book shows each wizard's purse, the century dial picks the Age, and the portal sets out. Next door, the Market's four counters haggle, and a sale leaves a coin pouch you carry home. Issues #312 to #314 and #355 to #360.

changes.alt: The Lair in Unity: a long table, strongboxes, a fireplace and the century dial
changes.caption: docs/art/models/lair/lair-unity.png

changes: keep
Built 7 October: the Market yard
Four stalls, a well and a cart.
The Market is reachable from the Lair, solo and in co-op. Nothing is hurt or broken there.
keep
Built 8 October: you play as a wizard
The capsule became a modelled, animated wizard.
Idle, walk, crouch and cast animations, checked in co-op so each player sees the other move. Issues #336, #361 and #362.

changes.alt: Model sheet of the wizard from several angles
changes.caption: docs/art/models/lair/wizard.png

changes: keep
Built 12 to 15 October: the Wick
The Lantern Warden drops his lantern and turns into the Wick.
Modelled with nine animations. In a raid the Wick stalks, hunts and catches players. Issues #406, #413 and #417, landed through #414 and #436.

changes.alt: Model sheet of the Wick with its stalk animation
changes.caption: docs/art/anim/fear/wick_stalk.png

changes: keep
Built 12 October: the Ophan of Hours, modelled
Three wheels of eyes, six wings and one great eye.
Modelled with five animations (#411, #412). It is the creature that owns you.

changes.alt: Model sheet of the Ophan of Hours
changes.caption: docs/art/models/fear/ophan.png

changes: keep
Built 18 October: loot in the Lair stays where you left it
The unsold haul is saved per save slot, each piece in its place.
It comes back after you quit and relaunch. Issue #378, landed through #422.

changes.alt: The Lair with loot on the floor by the table
changes.caption: docs/generated/lair-pile-2026-10-18/run1-host-after.png

changes: keep
Built 26 to 27 October: staging, all of the above tested together
The Wick, the fear art, the Lair save, the death fix and five-minute raids.

A player the Wick catches now dies on both machines, not only their own, and raids are five minutes from one tuning file (#433). Checks on staging: compile clean, 264 EditMode tests pass with 3 skipped, all 529 PlayMode tests pass, and the scripted co-op, Wick and raid-length checks pass. The staging pull request into main, #437, waits on your own co-op test by hand.

changes.alt: The portal and the pocket watch at the start of a five-minute raid
changes.caption: docs/generated/ophan-demand-tuning-433/staging-r1-watch-start.png

changes: new
Now, #418: the Ophan in the sky
It appears far beyond the castle in the last minute and hunts with beams.

About 60 seconds before the portal closes it appears 150 times its model's size with a loud hum and screen shake. Its eye follows whoever carries the most worth. After a three-second lock-on a slow beam drains health, and stone blocks it; a charged beam kills in one hit and scorches walls open; a beam on the artifact's carrier lifts the piece away and the Ophan leaves. Steps: #439 sky, hum and shake (built); #440 eye and rings (built); #441 slow beam (works; its look floods the target's view, shown here, and needs tuning); #442 charged beam (code and tests only); #443 wide-wing pose and #444 full checks and landing on staging (not started). Being built on your PC on AjsAgent/ophan-arrival-418.

before.alt: The Ophan rising above the curtain wall

after.alt: A huge white wedge of light covering the top of the screen

changes.caption: Arrival, then the slow beam's look that still needs tuning. docs/generated/ophan-418/solo-arrival.png and solo-beam.png

changes: new
Next, #419: the Ophan's demand
The coin debt and the Collector go; the Ophan demands one artifact.

The first demand is due at the end of your first raid and sits deep in the vault; after that one falls due every three to five raids. You recognise the piece by its sketch in the ledger. In your words: “The demand has nothing to do with progression. It holds off the beast, a deterrent but never the solution.”

changes.alt: The ledger book open on its lectern
changes.caption: docs/generated/ledger-book-2026-10-07/book-close.png: the ledger as it is today, where the demand's sketch will go

changes: new
Then, #435: playtest the demand loop
Solo first, then two players on your two PCs.
In your words: “The game must be fun solo, not only survivable.”
new
Later: upgrading
Coin buys counters to each Age's threats.

Spells, tools and weapons that counter each Age's threats, plus cosmetics and emotes. Worth goes up visibly so progress shows in steps. Frango is the first spell for a new save. Designed with you, one area at a time.
new
Later: lore and world-building
How you learn the Ophan can be beaten.
The Ophan starts undefeatable. Lore found in the world slowly reveals a weakness, without turning this into a narrative game.
new
Later: events
The world reacts to you, and some things just happen.

Plague rats spreading through the castle, the Ophan arriving early, a full moon that turns every enemy, an invasion through the front gate. Each event gets its own designed warning. In your words: “I want this world to feel alive, and dangerous, and for your actions to have clear consequences.”
new
Later: enemies
Each Age's threats need their own counters.
The environment always fights back, and each object needs its own strategy.
